decision: Test whether structural-originality or trading-semantic prefilters improve alpha-discovery efficiency before adding more complex memory, verifier, evolution, or adaptive-search machinery.
claim_boundary: This is a mechanism-level matched ablation on a fixed deterministic candidate generator. It does not reproduce AlphaAgent or AlphaSchema end-to-end and cannot by itself produce a BEAT/TIE/LOSE paper-family verdict.

arms.mechanism: reject a candidate before evaluation when its sign-invariant canonical expression AST fingerprint has already been evaluated
reject a candidate before evaluation when its operation + economic feature group + exact horizon schema has already been evaluated

dataset.source_window_note: Corrected after the first real-data run fail-closed on the stale prior rolling-window expectation. The observed owner-cache manifest was 2024-06-03 through 2026-06-01; no PIT universe, panel, candidate evaluation, validation metric, or OOS metric had executed before this correction.
dataset.universe: PIT Prime/Standard/Growth common stocks, top 256 by pre-cutoff mean adjusted price*volume after the existing history gate

split.boundary_rule: Use the first available panel trading day on/after each calendar boundary; OOS end is inclusive.
split.validation_use: one-day mean rank IC for finalist ranking
split.oos_use: read only after all arm candidates and finalists are frozen

generator.source_features: all backward-looking standardized features emitted by scripts/alphazerobeta_prepare.py
order: all positive single-feature expressions in panel feature order
all sign-reflected single-feature expressions in the same order
for each feature pair i<j: blend(i,j), blend(j,i), spread(i,j), spread(j,i)
generator.note: Sign reflection and commutative/reversed forms intentionally preserve generator redundancy; the experiment asks whether pre-evaluation gates convert that fixed redundancy into more useful evaluated candidates under equal evaluator-call budgets.

budget.same_model_backend: not applicable; generator is deterministic and model-free

primary_metric: unique untouched-OOS survivors per 24 validation evaluator calls
secondary_metrics: validation evaluator calls per unique OOS survivor

comparison_rule.mechanism_improves_primary: arm unique OOS survivor count is strictly greater than baseline under exactly 24 validation calls
comparison_rule.tie: same unique OOS survivor count as baseline
comparison_rule.worse: strictly fewer unique OOS survivors than baseline

anti_overfitting: No OOS result may change the pool order, fingerprints, schema definition, budget, finalist count, split, portfolio rule, costs, or survivor gate.
All three arms use the same candidate pool and the same train/validation/OOS panel.
Candidate orientation uses train data only.
Finalist selection uses validation data only.
OOS values are not used for candidate generation, gate decisions, orientation, or finalist selection.
A null or negative result is canonical evidence and does not trigger post-hoc parameter changes.
required_outputs: machine-readable result with every scanned/evaluated/rejected candidate and exact reason
